channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Nations League: Promising France defeat Belgium thanks to Olise
item.description: Following their victory in Turkey, France won away at Belgium (1-0). Thanks to this victory, Les Bleus are now at the top of Group A.
item.dc:creator: L'Equipe TV

item.title: OpenAI cancels release of new AI model over safety concerns
item.description: OpenAI will not release its latest artificial intelligence model, Astra 6.1, after internal tests found it fell short of safety standards, the ChatGPT maker confirmed on Monday. The decision comes ahead of its annual DevDay conference in San Francisco on Tuesday, where the company is expected to announce new products.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Argentina’s Milei threatens to sue UK over Falkland Islands oil project
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei threatened on Monday to sue Britain over the Sea Lion oil project near the disputed Falkland Islands. Argentina claims sovereignty over the British-administered territory, where a 1982 war killed 255 British and 649 Argentine troops. Developers Navitas and Rockhopper say they hold valid British-issued exploration licences.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: US prosecutors reopen Cornell university gang rape investigation
item.description: US prosecutors reopened an investigation on Monday into an alleged 2024 gang rape at Cornell University after the woman involved accused the school of failing to punish those responsible adequately. In a lawsuit, she said seven Chi Phi fraternity members drugged her with ketamine and assaulted her. Cornell closed the fraternity and expelled several students.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: French student protests fuel political clash ahead of 2027 presidential vote
item.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu and hard-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon traded barbs on Monday over high school students blockading classes to demand more resources. The students cite teacher shortages, deteriorating schools and heavy schedules. The dispute comes ahead of next spring’s presidential election and mounting pressure over France’s finances.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Evicted 87-year-old Spanish pensioner to return home after deal
item.description: An 87-year-old Madrid pensioner whose eviction became a rallying point for Spain’s housing protests will be able to return home after reaching a deal with the property’s owners, her lawyer said Monday. The agreement comes as demonstrations across the country pile pressure on Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s government to address soaring rents, a shortage of affordable homes and weak tenant protections.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Nations League: Italy rebound in Turkey as France snatch late win in Belgium
item.description: Italy bounced back in style on Monday, thumping Turkey 4-1 in the rain to revive their Nations League campaign, while France edged Belgium 1-0 in Brussels with a late winner from Michael Olise. Elsewhere, Sweden beat Poland 3-1, Bosnia and Herzegovina overcame Romania 4-2, and Northern Ireland held Hungary to a goalless draw.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Expert says UK airbase plot 'fits into a very intense pattern we've been seeing in past two months'
item.description: British police said Monday five men arrested near an airbase used by the United States were released on bail, as officers probed whether a "foreign state" could be involved in a suspected bomb plot. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Monte Francis, Yan Saint-Pierre, CEO of Modern Security Consulting Group, explains that many of the hybrid warfare cases seen recently "involve local nationals, this is not about exporting terror" adding that foreign actors aim to have "as many layers as possible to complicate any investigation and accurate denounciation of culprits".
item.dc:creator: Monte FRANCIS

item.title: RAF Fairford: AI-enhanced photos of suspects fuel false claims about their religion
item.description: Five men arrested over a suspected bomb plot at RAF Fairford have been released on bail as investigations continue. Meanwhile, AI-enhanced images purporting to show their faces have gone viral, with some users claiming it ‘proves’ the men are Muslim. SynthID confirms the sharpened images were created using OpenAI tools, meaning the AI has suggested different facial features. UK police have not disclosed any names or religion, only that the men are all British nationals. Vedika Bahl explains.
item.dc:creator: Vedika BAHL

item.title: France braces for a day of strikes and protests over civil servants' pay
item.description: Trade unions in France have called on public sector workers - from train drivers to teachers to health workers and police officers - to stop working and protest at the government's plan to freeze the public sector's pay index, just days before the government is set to unveil its draft budget for 2027. Plus, as Paris Fashion Week kicks off, we speak with an expert on what the struggling luxury sector needs to do towards a more sustainable future.
item.dc:creator: Yuka ROYER

item.title: Ethiopian forces claim Tigray town
item.description: In tonight's edition, Ethiopia's army says it's seized a key city in the northern region of Tigray amidst escalating conflict with local rebels. Also, two mass shootings in South Africa leave at least 28 dead. And Ugandan activist Praise Aloikin Opoloje is facing court after she turned up following days of uncertainty about her whereabouts.
item.dc:creator: Georja CALVIN-SMITH

item.title: French far-right's Bardella denies alleged 2013 antisemitic comments as Le Pen sees boost in polls
item.description: A French investigative website on Monday alleged that far-right National Rally leader Jordan Bardella made antisemitic comments in writing in 2013, but the close ally of presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen dismissed the claims as fake. The allegations emerged as Le Pen's prospects for the 2027 elections appear stronger than at any point in her previous campaigns. FRANCE 24's Jennie Shin speaks with Dr Andrew Smith, Lecturer in History and Liberal Arts at Queen Mary University of London.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Ukrainian arms producers warn competitive edge eroding due to stringent export licence rules
item.description: Russian drones struck Ukraine's National Academy of Sciences in the historic heart of Kyiv on Monday, in the latest deadly daytime attack on the capital. Volodymyr Zelensky has long been pleading with Ukraine’s allies for more military aid to fend off Russia. But Ukrainian weapons producers say the country could be bringing in significant revenue of its own, if only they were allowed to export their products. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Kyiv.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Leo the moderate? Pope in France defends EU values
item.description: There's a new Pope in town and he's got very different ideas on what France's far-right calls the defense of Christian civilization. Leo the 14th concluding his trip to France in the eastern city of Metz, hometown of a founding father of present-day European federalism Maurice Schumann. There, the head of the world's largest organized religion proudly stated fact, that Europe’s roots are Christian, dating back to the Romans, all the while hailing an EU model that transcends 'us versus them' ideology, which brushes aside ‘might is right’ in favor of human rights and international law.
item.dc:creator: François PICARD

item.title: Trump ‘flips & flops’ with Iran between making a deal and threats to attack in ‘devastating fashion’
item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Barbara Slavin, Distinguished Fellow at the Stimson Center. She describes the US-Iran conflict as a dangerous combination of military escalation, diplomatic ambiguity and political calculation. Slavin sees an absence of true diplomacy: The recent indirect contacts between Washington and Tehran, mediated by Qatar, has been too limited and too fragile to produce any serious breakthrough. For her, this amounts to “kabuki diplomacy”: they half engage while positioning themselves against any appearance of compromise.
item.dc:creator: François PICARD

item.title: US deportations are triggering a 'cascade' of rights abuses, UN experts warn
item.description: The Trump administration's policy of deportating thousands of people to countries with which they have no links is "increasing risks of torture and ill-treatment and enforced disappearance", a panel of independent UN experts warned on Monday. An investigation by an international consortium of journalists including FRANCE 24 reporters determined last week that more than 25,000 third-country nationals had been deported by the end of August.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: 🔴 Pope Leo leaves France after ending four-day visit with plea for Europe to foster global dialogue
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France puts out massive fire that torched 42,000 hectares and smouldered for 69 days
item.description: France's largest wildfire since 1949 has been declared extinguished more than two months after it broke out in southwestern Gironde, forcing the evacuation of around 224,000 people and covering the city of Bordeaux with a thick plume of smoke. The blaze was put under control on August 1, but continued to smoulder underground for weeks.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Israel's opposition bloc, Netanyahu’s coalition in dead heat, election poll finds
item.description: With a month to go until Israel goes to the polls on October 27th, a new opinion poll shows the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party in a dead heat with Prime Minister Benyamin Netanyahu's coalition. It comes as the leaders of the four main opposition parties pledged to work together.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Tigray TV station hit by drone as rebels advance in north Ethiopia
item.description: Authorities in Ethiopia are accusing outside forces of backing armed groups fighting the country's troops in the north. Since last week, heavy clashes have been reported between government forces and the Tigray people's liberation front.It's raised fears of a wider regional conflict erupting. Delano D'Souza explains
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: As midterms approach, does GOP have a Trump problem?
item.description: The US midterm elections are just five weeks away - and while the US President is not on the ballot, his influence is top of mind for Republicans. Donald Trump's approval ratings have been hitting record lows in recent weeks, and in a sign of the party's concern it has started pouring campaign funding into many seats once considered safe, and some candidates have even changed their tune on one of the election's biggest issues: The US's war in Iran.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: French hotels, souvenir shops benefit from pope business boost
item.description: Monday is the final day of Pope Leo'svisit to France and the trip has been marked not only by an outpouring of emotion from France's Catholics but also flurry of economic activity. The first figures are beginning to come in from the pope's trip, and unsurprisingly, they're showing a big boost in tourism activity related to his appearances - with hotels and restaurants in and around the cities he's visited getting a particular benefit.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Five suspects arrested in explosives case near UK airbase were British nationals
item.description: Five suspects arrested by British police on suspicion of terrorism and explosives ​offenses after white vans drove towards an airbase used by US forces were all British nationals from London in their early 20s, police said on Monday. France 24 Benedicte Paviot has more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24
